architecture.mechanism: Zwitterionic surface chemistry to suppress biofouling and scale formation via strong hydration and charge regulation
architecture.intervention: Graft zwitterionic polymer brushes (e.g., poly(carboxybetaine methacrylate)) onto lead RO membranes to create a hydrated, charge-neutral interface that repels organic foulants and inhibits mineral scaling
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced biofouling and scale accumulation, maintaining normalized differential pressure within 5% over 6 weeks while preserving ≥45% permeate recovery
architecture.falsification_test: Measure differential pressure increase in a pilot-scale RO train with zwitterionic-grafted membranes vs. untreated controls under identical feedwater conditions (TDS, turbidity, microbial load) for 6 weeks; confirm <5% ΔP increase and <10% flux decline in treated membranes
